name: Form Shooting
cues: Elbow under the ball, wrist straight back
Rise up through your legs first
Snap wrist down, fingers point at the rim
Hold follow-through until the ball hits
description: Close-range shooting (3–8 ft) focusing purely on mechanics. Perfect for daily warm-up.

name: 1-Dribble Pull-Up
cues: Pound dribble with purpose, not timid
Gather with both hands simultaneously
Jump straight up — no drift
Quick, high release
description: Attack the mid-range off one decisive dribble. Trains the gather-to-shot transition.

name: Catch & Shoot
cues: Catch in your shot pocket — don't dip
Feet already set when the ball arrives
Shoot on the way up, not at the top
Eyes on the front of the rim
description: Spot-up shooting from 5 positions around the arc. Focuses on quick-release mechanics.

name: Free Throws Under Fatigue
cues: Breathe out, slow your HR before shooting
Same pre-shot routine every time
Trust the process — don't aim, shoot
Bounce ball the same number of times
description: Sprint, then immediately shoot two free throws. Trains game-realistic FT pressure.

name: 3PT Around the World
cues: Move at your shot-making speed, not just fast
Reset footwork at each spot
Track makes — compete with yourself
Don't let a miss rush the next shot
description: 7 spots around the 3-point line, 5 shots each. Builds three-point volume and consistency.

name: Steph Curry Warm-Up Series
cues: Layups → short pull-ups → 3s in progression
Never stop moving between shots
Catch and go — minimize setup time
Keep track of your make % each session
description: Layup → mid-range → three-pointer circuit. Progressive warm-up that builds rhythm.

name: Elbow Jumpers
cues: Attack the elbow at game speed
Jump stop into your shot — no extra dribbles
Keep shooting shoulder pointed at the rim
Maintain arc even on tired legs
description: Mid-range pull-ups from both elbows. A high-efficiency shot every player needs.

name: Off-Screen Catch & Shoot
cues: Set up the defender with a curl fake
Explode off the screen shoulder
Catch in your pocket, shoot in one motion
Stay low through the cut, rise to shoot
description: Use cones as screens. Simulates catching off a screen in game situations.

name: Step-Backs
cues: Drive first — make the defender commit
Step back on balance — two feet together
Load and fire quickly, no extra gather
Land where you took off from
description: Create space with a backward gather step. One of the most dangerous modern shots.

name: Floaters
cues: Release before the help defender arrives
High arc — aim for the top of the backboard
One or two feet — both are valid
Soft touch: wrist, not arm
description: Tear-drop shots in the paint to score over shot-blockers.

name: Mid-Range Pull-Ups
cues: Attack aggressively, stop on a dime
Stay low in your gather — don't stand up early
Quick release — defenders recover fast
Finish with full follow-through
description: Pull-up jumpers from 15–18 ft. The most reliable shot in clutch moments.

name: Deep Threes
cues: Use your legs — deep shots need more power
Same mechanics as your normal 3, not a heave
Practice from logo range + 2 feet back
Only shoot when your form doesn't break down
description: Beyond the arc shooting from NBA/college distance. Range expansion work.

name: Stationary 2-Ball Dribble
cues: Keep head up — no looking at the ball
Pound both balls simultaneously
Low stance — stay athletic
Relax your grip, use your fingertips
description: Simultaneous and alternating two-ball dribbling in place. Builds coordination and touch.

name: Figure 8s
cues: Wide stance, low center of gravity
Pass cleanly between legs — no slaps
Gradually increase speed each set
Try both directions — forward and backward
description: Thread the ball in a figure-8 pattern through and around your legs.

name: Tennis Ball Drops
cues: Eyes on the tennis ball, not the basketball
React fast — catch before second bounce
Keep the dribble rhythm intact while catching
Mix dominant and off hand catching
description: Dribble while reacting to a dropped tennis ball. Trains eyes-up dribbling and reaction.

name: Cone Weaves
cues: Stay low — don't pop up between cones
Push the ball ahead of you, don't carry it
Mix crossover, between legs, behind back
First step explosive out of each cone
description: Dribble through a cone course with various dribble moves at each cone.

name: In-and-Outs
cues: Sell the crossover with your shoulders
Snapping motion — quick and decisive
Alternate hands each set
Use in combo: in-and-out → crossover
description: Fake crossover that keeps the ball on the same side. Essential deception move.

name: Crossover Series
cues: Low crossover — protect the ball
Shift your weight with the ball
Explode the first step after the cross
Vary speed: slow → quick → explosive
description: Front crossover variations: basic, low, hesitation cross, and between-legs entry.

name: Behind-the-Back Series
cues: Sweep ball across your lower back, not high
Lead foot points in the new direction
Practice stationary before adding movement
Don't look back at the ball
description: Behind-the-back dribble mastery: stationary, walking, and at speed.

name: Between-Legs Combos
cues: Step forward as ball goes through
Alternate legs — both directions
Combine: between legs → crossover
Build speed progressively
description: Between-the-leg dribble variations and combinations at increasing speed.

name: Full-Court Speed Dribble
cues: Push ball out in front at full speed
Eyes up — see the whole court
Finish with a layup or pull-up
Change hands at half-court
description: End-to-end dribble at max speed finishing with a shot. Conditioning + handles.

name: Hesitation Moves
cues: Slow → BURST — the contrast is the move
Stand up slightly during the hesi to freeze defender
Explode past immediately — don't waste the fake
Read defender: if they bite, blow by; if not, pull up
description: Hesi dribble at full speed to freeze defenders before blowing by.

name: Mikan Drill
cues: Alternate sides with each rep
Jump off inside foot on each side
High off the glass — don't bank hard
Keep the rhythm: catch, one step, up
description: Alternating baby hooks on both sides of the basket. The classic finishing drill.

name: Reverse Mikan
cues: Stay under the basket the whole time
Reverse lay-in softly off the board
Keep ball high — don't drop it
Quick off both feet each jump
description: Mikan variation: reverse layups on both sides. Trains ambidextrous finishing.

name: Euro Steps
cues: Plant first foot hard to set direction
Big lateral step — make defender commit
Keep ball protected and low during the step
Finish off two feet or one depending on angle
description: Two-step gather that sidesteps defenders. A must-have in the modern game.

name: Floaters Off Two Feet
cues: Jump stop, then release immediately
Push ball up fast before defender arrives
Arc it — don't laser it
Both hands steady on the ball until release
description: Two-foot floater for compact guards. Hard to block and effective in traffic.

name: Finishing Through Contact
cues: Brace your core before contact hits
Keep eyes on the target — don't flinch
Finish high — don't bring ball down after contact
And-1 mentality: score then react
description: Attack the basket while a partner applies pad contact. Builds physicality at the rim.

name: Off-Hand Layups
cues: Drive from the right, finish left (and vice versa)
Trust the off hand — don't switch back
Practice the gather on the correct foot
Soft touch: think 'place it up' not 'throw it'
description: Layups with the non-dominant hand from multiple angles. Eliminates a predictable weakness.

name: Runners
cues: Release early — before the shot-blocker jumps
High, looping arc over the defense
Push off your outside foot for balance
One hand finish — keep it simple
description: Running one-hand push shots in the paint from various angles.

name: Reverse Layups
cues: Use the basket as your shot-blocker shield
Swing under and up in one motion
Soft touch off the glass, not the front rim
Jump slightly past the basket to create angle
description: Come-from-behind layups using the backboard to protect from help defenders.

name: Jump Stops
cues: Land both feet at the same time
Bend knees on landing — absorb impact
Stay balanced — don't lean forward
Either foot can be your pivot after
description: Controlled two-foot stops after a dribble drive or receive. Foundation of footwork.

name: Pivot Drills
cues: Pivot foot stays — don't drag it
Use both front and reverse pivots
Stay low and balanced during the pivot
Swing free foot around, not just your body
description: Front pivot and reverse pivot mastery. Enables ball reversal and drive creation.

name: Drop Steps
cues: Pin defender on your hip before the drop
Big step baseline with your trail foot
Power dribble to the block, then finish
Keep ball high — don't let defender strip
description: Post-up footwork: establish position, drop step baseline, and power through for a finish.

name: Jab Series
cues: Quick, sharp jab step — make it real
Read defender: if they step back, shoot; if they hold, drive
Triple threat position before every jab
Stay on the balls of your feet
description: Jab-step sequences: jab-shoot, jab-drive, jab-crossover. Master the first action.

name: Triple Threat Reads
cues: Ball on your hip, ready to shoot, pass, or drive
Stay low — don't stand upright
Read the cone (defender) before deciding
React, don't pre-decide
description: Read a simulated defender and choose the correct action: shoot, drive, or pass.

name: Closeout Slides
cues: Sprint then chop steps as you close out
Low and wide on the chop — don't fly by
Hands up, not reaching in
Land in defensive stance, ready to slide
description: Closeout technique: sprint approach + chop steps + defensive stance. Prevents blow-bys.

name: Defensive Slides
cues: Don't let feet come together
Stay in your stance — don't stand up
Push off the trailing foot
Mirror: move before the ball does
description: Side-to-side defensive movement maintaining proper stance. Core defensive conditioning.

name: Closeout Drill
cues: High hands on the run in
Chop steps at 3 feet from the ball
Don't reach — stay disciplined
Force baseline, not middle
description: Close out on a shooter from the help position. Balances contest with blow-by prevention.

name: Mirror Drill
cues: Stay square to your partner
React to movement, don't guess
Keep your stance — don't cross your feet
Compete: try to step on their foot
description: 1-on-1 mirroring drill without a ball. Builds lateral quickness and defensive anticipation.

name: Deny Stance
cues: Ball-you-man alignment at all times
Lead hand in the passing lane
See both the ball and your man
Move on the catch, not after
description: Off-ball denial positioning and footwork. Learn to influence cuts and deny passes.

name: Rebounding Box-Outs
cues: Find your man first — then find the ball
Make contact before spinning in
Low and wide — be immovable
Chin the ball with elbows out after you get it
description: Box-out technique on missed shots. Establishes physical positioning for every rebound.

name: Suicides
cues: Touch each line with your hand
Accelerate out of each direction change
Breathe on the way back — recover fast
Don't slow down on the last sprint
description: Classic court sprint conditioning: baseline to each line and back. Basketball staple.

name: 17s
cues: 17 sideline-to-sideline sprints in under 60s
Touch each line with your foot
Stay relaxed — tension kills speed
Push hardest on the last 5
description: 17 sideline sprints in 60 seconds. The NBA combine conditioning benchmark.

name: Lane Slides
cues: Stay in defensive stance the whole time
Don't let feet touch — constant movement
Hips low, back straight
Increase speed each set
description: Defensive slide across the paint repeatedly. Combines conditioning with defensive footwork.

name: 3-Man Weave (Solo)
cues: Sprint behind after your 'pass' (dribble hand-off)
Hit the sideline on each weave
Finish with a layup at full speed
Come back with a dribble, weave again
description: Solo simulation of the 3-man weave. Full-court cardio + finishing at speed.

name: Shuttle Runs
cues: Quick change of direction — don't round the cone
Stay low in the change of direction
Drive arms to accelerate
Record time and beat it each week
description: Short-distance acceleration and deceleration training with cones.

name: Line Touches
cues: Touch the floor with your hand — full range
Low, quick, explosive out of each touch
Compete: beat your previous count
Keep your head up between touches
description: Touch multiple lines as fast as possible. Agility + work capacity builder.

name: Pickup Game Simulation
cues: Sprint every transition — both ways
Play defense like someone is watching
Treat every possession like it matters
Mix shooting drills in during dead balls
description: Solo full-court simulation: sprint, shoot, rebound, repeat. Game-speed conditioning.

name: Ladder Drills
cues: Quick feet — don't look down at the ladder
Stay on the balls of your feet
Pump your arms with your legs
Mix patterns: in-in-out-out, Ickey shuffle, 2-in
description: Agility ladder patterns for foot speed, coordination, and conditioning.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
cues: Hips hinge back — not a squat
Chest up, neutral spine throughout
Drive the floor away — push, don't pull
Lockout glutes hard at the top
description: Lower body strength foundation. Builds power for jumping and explosive first steps.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
cues: Rear foot elevated, front foot far enough forward
Knee tracks over toe — don't cave in
Lower with control — 3-second descent
Drive through front heel to stand
description: Unilateral leg strength. Fixes imbalances and directly transfers to one-leg jumping.

name: Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
cues: Hinge at the hips — minimal knee bend
Bar stays close to your legs the whole way
Feel the stretch in your hamstrings
Squeeze glutes aggressively at the top
description: Posterior chain strength and hamstring hypertrophy. Injury prevention + power.

name: Goblet Squat
cues: Hold dumbbell at chest height
Elbows inside knees at the bottom
Squat to parallel or below
Torso stays upright — don't fold over
description: Beginner-friendly squat for leg strength and mobility. Great for home gym.

name: Single-Leg RDL
cues: Hinge on one leg — other leg floats back
Keep hips square — don't rotate
Slow and controlled — fight the balance
Feel the hamstring stretch on the standing leg
description: Unilateral posterior chain work. Builds stability and strength for single-leg landings.

name: Broad Jumps
cues: Load hips back before you jump
Jump as far as possible — max effort
Land soft — absorb through hips and knees
Reset fully before each rep
description: Horizontal power training. Measures and builds explosive lower body strength.

name: Depth Jumps
cues: Step off — don't jump off the box
Minimal ground contact time — hair-trigger
Jump as high as possible immediately on landing
Land through the balls of your feet, not heels
description: Reactive strength plyometric. Step down, instantly jump up. Elite vertical training.

name: Med Ball Slams
cues: Full extension overhead before slamming
Slam with your whole body — not just arms
Hinge to pick it up — protect your back
Exhale explosively on every slam
description: Full-body power + conditioning. Builds overhead strength and explosive hip extension.

name: Lateral Bounds
cues: Push off one foot — land on the opposite
Stick the landing for 2 seconds before bounding back
Jump as wide as possible — not just quick
Stay low and athletic on each landing
description: Lateral plyometric power. Trains the same muscles used in defensive slides and cuts.

name: Nordic Curls
cues: Slow eccentric — take 3–4 seconds to lower
Catch yourself with hands at the bottom
Pull back up using your hamstrings, not arms
Keep hips extended — don't fold at the waist
description: Most effective hamstring injury prevention exercise. Hard but essential.

name: Calf Raises
cues: Full range: all the way down, all the way up
Pause 1 second at the top — no bouncing
Single-leg variation is more effective
Add weight when 20 reps feel easy
description: Calf and Achilles tendon strength. Critical for jump height and ankle injury prevention.

name: Kevin Durant Mid-Range Series
cues: Use your height — shoot over the defense
Quick, high release with consistent touch
Attack the high post, receive and shoot
Fade slightly when defender is close
description: High-post and elbow mid-range series. Develop the signature KD fadeaway and straight-line pull-up.

name: Shooting Off the Dribble Handoff
cues: Attack the handoff aggressively, don't drift
Use your body to rip through the handoff
Be ready to shoot or drive based on defense
Footwork must be a 1-2 step into the shot
description: Simulate dribble hand-off (DHO) actions with cones. Builds catching in traffic and quick-release skills.

name: Spot Up Shooting — 5 Spots
cues: Establish your base before the catch
Hip rotation initiates the shot
Same pre-shot routine every time
Track your make percentage at each spot
description: 5 spots around the arc: corners, wings, and top. The foundation of any shooting workout.

name: Shooting on the Move — Curl Cuts
cues: Curl tight around the cone (screen)
Eyes to the passer as you come off
Catch and square up in one fluid motion
Shoot off the curl, not after drifting
description: Simulate curling off screens with cone routes. Essential for off-ball players.

name: Mikan Drill
cues: Use the backboard on both sides
Soft touch — don't power the ball in
Alternate sides with no wasted steps
Work on weak hand exclusively if needed
description: Alternating layups on each side of the rim. Builds soft hands and interior scoring touch.

name: Post Fade and Drop Step
cues: Establish deep post position first
Read the defense before making your move
Fade: create distance, stay balanced
Drop step: two quick power dribbles, strong finish
description: Post scoring fundamentals: fade-away jumper and drop step power move.

name: Figure-8 Dribbling
cues: Keep the ball below knee height
Quick hands — don't let the ball sit
Low athletic stance throughout
Speed up each set to improve
description: Weave the ball in a figure-8 around your legs. Builds ambidextrous handle and coordination.

name: Dribble Attack Series
cues: Explode into each move like it's a defender
Change of pace before the move
Protect the ball with your body on attacks
Finish at the rim each time
description: 5-cone attack series: crossover, between legs, behind back, spin, hesitation.

name: Tennis Ball Dribbling
cues: Catch the tennis ball before it hits ground
Never look down at the basketball
Throw tennis ball to yourself at different heights
Focus eyes at horizon level
description: Dribble a basketball while catching/throwing a tennis ball. Trains heads-up dribbling.

name: Two-Ball Dribbling
cues: Both balls bounce simultaneously at first
Alternate the bounces when comfortable
Keep both balls at equal height
Never let either ball die — constant motion
description: Dribble two basketballs simultaneously — same time and alternating. Builds elite ambidextrous control.

name: Hesitation (Hesi) Move
cues: Slow down before the hesi to freeze defender
Reset your weight back, then explode forward
Show the ball slightly — bait the reach
Drive past them low and fast
description: Master the hesitation dribble to freeze defenders. One of the most effective moves off the dribble.

name: Between the Legs Combo
cues: Stay low — bent knees throughout
Push the ball through, don't flip it
Front-back foot position for each between-legs
Chain into crossovers and behind-the-back
description: Between-the-legs combination moves. Build the confidence to execute under pressure.

name: Chair Dribbling Series
cues: Use cones as defenders — react to them
Read the cone: go left or right based on position
Push the pace — move at game speed
Use a different move at each cone
description: Navigate through 4-5 cones using different dribble moves. Simulates game-like decision-making.

name: Euro Step Layup
cues: Gather on one side, step wide to the other
Use your body to shield the ball from defenders
Go up off the outside foot
Soft release at the top of your jump
description: Two-step lateral finishing move to avoid shot-blockers. Master both left and right.

name: Floater Finish
cues: Release the ball before reaching the rim
Use your wrist and fingertips — gentle touch
Slight arc — not flat, not too high
Practice from 8-14 feet on both sides
description: The teardrop floater over big defenders. Essential for guards and wings driving the lane.

name: Reverse Layup
cues: Go under the basket, flip from the other side
Use the rim as a protector from shot-blockers
Soft touch — let the backboard help
Inside hand for reverse, off the glass
description: Finishing from below the rim using the backboard for protection. Hard to block when done correctly.

name: Up-and-Under Move
cues: Show the ball high to make defender jump
Step through as they commit
Go up strong with two feet when possible
Sell the first fake completely
description: Fake a shot, draw the block attempt, step through for the easy finish. A classic post move.

name: Contact Finishing
cues: Attack through contact — don't fade away
Absorb the hit in your core and legs
Stay strong — don't let contact kill momentum
Finish high and strong through the bump
description: Practice absorbing contact and still finishing at the rim. Use a pad or partner to simulate defenders.

name: Drop Step Footwork
cues: Pivot on your pivot foot, swing leg drops wide
Get low on the drop — create a wide base
Power dribble before the finish
Practice from both sides of the post
description: The drop step footwork pattern. Used in the post and high-low game to gain position.

name: L-Cut Footwork
cues: Plant hard on the direction-change foot
Cut at 90 degrees — not a rounded curve
Explode off the cut like sprinting
Hands ready for the pass as you come free
description: The L-cut for receiving passes. Sharp cuts create separation from defenders.

name: Three-Threat Position Drills
cues: Ball in shot pocket — ready to shoot, pass, or drive
Slight shoulder fake to test the defense
Low center of gravity — bounce on your toes
Eyes on the rim, use peripheral vision for defense
description: Establish and read from the triple-threat position. Every catch should start here.

name: Swing Step and Drive
cues: Jab step to probe the defender
If they don't react, cross and go
Keep the jab low and out
Drive with purpose — straight to the rim
description: Jab step series with drive finishes. The most fundamental 1v1 footwork pattern.

name: Pivot Work
cues: Keep pivot foot grounded — no traveling
Swing on the ball of your foot
Use front and reverse pivots to create angles
Keep ball protected during the pivot
description: Front and reverse pivots to create passing and shooting angles. Footwork fundamentals.

name: Closeout Footwork
cues: Sprint to half-distance, then chop steps
Hands up — contest without leaving feet
Land in a defensive stance, ready to slide
Don't fly by — controlled closeout
description: Sprint and chop-step closeout to an imaginary shooter. Most important defensive skill.

name: On-Ball Defensive Slides
cues: Stay in a wide, low stance
Push off the outside foot to slide
Feet never cross — step-slide pattern
Keep your nose on the ball
description: Lateral defensive footwork drill. Foundation of perimeter defense.

name: Help-Side Rotations
cues: Open stance — see ball and your man simultaneously
React to ball movement with active feet
Communicate 'help' or 'deny' verbally
Sprint to help position before the drive arrives
description: Practice rotating to help-side defensive positions using cones as ball and man markers.

name: Block and Contest
cues: Time the jump — don't leave too early
Go straight up — no swinging arms
Keep your hand up after missing the block
Body vertical to avoid fouls
description: Practice contesting shots by jumping vertically. Timed on-ball shot contests.

name: Deny Denial Defense
cues: Hand in the passing lane at all times
Stay between your man and the ball
React to back-cuts with instant rotation
Maintain denial without fouling
description: Practice denying the ball to a wing player, then recovering on cuts.

name: Suicides (Line Drills)
cues: Sprint — not jog — to each line
Touch the line with your hand
Turn using the inside foot to plant
Track your time and compete with it
description: Classic basketball conditioning drill: sprint to each court line in sequence.

name: 17s (Full-Court Sprints)
cues: Complete 17 sideline-to-sideline runs in 60 seconds
Run in a straight line — don't weave
Touch each sideline before turning
This is your conditioning benchmark
description: 17 sideline sprints in 60 seconds. The gold standard conditioning test for basketball.

name: 3-Man Weave Running
cues: Pass before you cross midline
Fill the outside lane at full speed
Catch in stride — no slowing down for the ball
Finish with a layup each time
description: Classic fast-break running drill. Builds conditioning, passing in stride, and finishing.

name: Continuous Jump Rope
cues: Stay on the balls of your feet
Small, quick jumps — not big hops
Relax shoulders, arms move from wrists
Breathe rhythmically with your jumps
description: Continuous rope jumping builds foot speed, rhythm, and aerobic capacity.

name: Defensive Slide Circuit
cues: Defensive stance throughout — no standing up
Explode laterally at each cone
Don't let your feet come together
Finish every rep even when tired
description: Defensive slides through a cone pattern. Combines conditioning with defensive footwork.

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
cues: Hinge at the hip — not a squat
Keep back flat and hip square
Feel the stretch in your hamstring
Control the eccentric — 2-3 seconds down
description: Unilateral hamstring and hip hinge strength. Addresses left-right imbalances and reduces injury risk.

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
cues: Front foot takes 90% of the load
Lower until back knee nearly touches
Keep torso upright — don't lean forward
Drive through front heel to stand
description: The most effective single-leg strength exercise. Builds quad and glute power without spine loading.

name: Med Ball Rotational Throws
cues: Drive rotation from hips, not arms
Explosive release — don't hold back
Catch and control before next rep
Throw both ways: left and right
description: Rotational power training for shot creation, passing velocity, and athletic movement.

name: Pull-Ups and Chin-Ups
cues: Full range: dead hang to chin over bar
No kipping — strict reps only for strength
Engage lats before pulling
Control the descent — 2 seconds down
description: Upper body pulling strength for rebounding, shot-blocking, and overall athleticism.

name: Resistance Band Hip Walks
cues: Band above knees in defensive stance
Keep tension in the band — step wide
Never let knees cave inward
Maintain quarter-squat depth throughout
description: Glute activation with resistance bands. Prevents knee valgus and improves lateral power.

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
cues: Set your back before lifting — big breath
Drive through your heels, extend hips and knees together
Bar stays close to your body throughout
Full lockout at top — don't hyperextend
description: The safest and most sport-specific version of the deadlift. Builds total-body strength for basketball.

name: Single-Leg Box Jumps
cues: Load on one leg, explode vertically
Land softly — absorb with bent knee
Step down, don't jump down
Rest 30 seconds between each rep
description: Unilateral explosive power development. Critical for one-foot take-off in layups and dunks.

name: Core Anti-Rotation Press
cues: Band at chest height, perpendicular to it
Press straight out — resist rotation
Engage core before pressing
Hold 2 seconds at full extension
description: The Pallof press builds rotational core stability. Protects spine and improves athletic bracing.

name: Farmer's Carry
cues: Stand tall — no leaning to either side
Grip the weight firmly without tensing shoulder
Breathe steadily with each step
Walk in a straight line at a controlled pace
description: Loaded carry for grip, core, and total-body strength. Build the foundation for all other lifts.

name: Gasser Runs
cues: Sprint baseline to baseline and back twice
Aim for sub-30 seconds each gasser
Rest 60-90 seconds between reps
Maintain form even when winded
description: Full-court sprint conditioning. Builds anaerobic capacity specific to basketball.

name: Machine Gun Feet
cues: Fast feet in place — quicker each set
Stay on balls of feet throughout
React to coach's signal to change direction
Keep a slightly forward-leaning athletic stance
description: Rapid in-place footwork drill for foot speed and reaction time.

name: Shell Drill (Team Defense)
cues: All 4 defenders maintain proper spacing
Ball moves: everyone rotates accordingly
Communicate every movement out loud
On-ball defender: make the ball handler uncomfortable
description: 4v4 defensive positioning drill. The standard team defense development exercise.

name: Weak Hand Finishing Circuit
cues: Never use your strong hand in this drill
Finger roll, backboard layup, and power finish with weak hand only
Go at 70% speed to build comfort
Form matters more than speed here
description: Dedicated weak-hand finishing circuit. Eliminating the weak hand is a game-changer.

name: Pull-Back Crossover
cues: Pound dribble, then pull back with crossover
Change of pace is the key — slow then fast
Keep the ball below your waist
Eyes up at all times
description: Pull back to reset, then attack with a crossover. Creates space from aggressive defenders.

name: Free Throw Routine Building
cues: Same routine every single rep — build the habit
One breath to reset before each shot
Focus on the front of the rim
Exaggerate follow-through to build muscle memory
description: Build a locked-in free throw routine. Consistency at the line wins close games.

name: Aggressive Catch and Square
cues: Catch moving toward the passer
Square shoulders to the basket immediately
Land in your shot pocket — ready to shoot
Read the defense as you catch
description: Practice catching and squaring up to the basket in one fluid motion.
